The term "naive empiricist" is not an accurate description of Austin; rather, it reflects his sophisticated development of ordinary language philosophy which moved beyond simple observation to analyze the logical structure and social functions of speech acts. His work demonstrated a deep understanding that meaning arises from context and usage within specific forms of life, challenging simplistic empirical views by emphasizing the normative rules governing our linguistic practices. Therefore, labeling him as naive overlooks his rigorous contributions to pragmatics and the philosophy of language.
